cohort: The study included 170 women diagnosed with pre-eclampsia attending obstetric units at four hospitals in Douala, Cameroon.
finding: Women with early onset pre-eclampsia (EOPE) had worse short-term outcomes, including higher odds of acute kidney injury and HELLP syndrome, and lower odds of deliveries without perinatal adverse events, compared with those with late onset pre-eclampsia (LOPE).
